title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts & API Examples — Docs Site Operating Procedures and Support Playbook
author: Ava Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose
This document provides the canonical developer-experience (DevEx) playbook for SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the top support issues with canonical fixes. It is intended for engineers, technical writers, and solutions engineers who author or maintain customer-facing developer docs.

Scope
- SDK guides (Type-safe examples, authentication, error handling)
- Quickstarts & templates (language-specific, integration recipes)
- API examples (REST + SDK + streaming patterns)
- Docs site operating procedures (publishing, review, versioning, rollouts)
- Top support issues and canonical fixes (triage-first responses and persistent remediations)

Ownership & Contacts
- Primary owner: DevEx Engineering (owner_team: engineering)
- Content lead: Ava Patel (author)
- Reviewers: James Li, Mariana Gomez, Owen Clarke
- Slack channel: #devex-docs
- Pager for incidents impacting docs-site: #platform-oncall

Document structure
1. Quickstarts & templates (by language and use-case)
2. SDK guides (patterns, auth, retries, pagination)
3. API examples (REST + streaming + function calling)
4. Docs site operating procedures (PR checklist, release cadence)
5. Top support issues and canonical fixes (triage guide + fixes)

1) Quickstarts & templates
Goal: Give a developer a working end-to-end integration in <30 minutes. Provide 3 artifacts per quickstart: README (overview + prerequisites), minimal runnable example, and a full example with tests. Maintain language parity for primary languages (Python, Node, Go, Java).

Required quickstart sections (template)
- Title and one-line summary
- Prerequisites (account, API keys, SDK version)
- Getting started (3-step quick path)
- Full example (recommended app structure)
- Tests & CI guidance (how to run)
- Troubleshooting (top 5 failures and fixes)

Example quickstart list (canonical)
- text-generation-quickstart (Python, Node)
- streaming-chat-quickstart (JS/TS streaming + chunking tips)
- embeddings-search-template (Python + Postgres vector store)
- reranking-pipeline-template (Node + serverless)

2) SDK guides: standards and examples
Standards
- Include an "Authentication" section showing environment variable and explicit client construction examples.
- Include error handling best practices with example retry/exponential backoff pseudocode.
- Document versioned client constructor signatures and migration notes.
- Always include snippets for both sync and async usage where applicable.

Auth example (Python)
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
response = client.generate("Write a short haiku about latency")
```

Retry guidance (pseudocode)
1. For 5xx and 429: retry with exponential backoff (initial=200ms, multiplier=2, max=8s) up to 5 attempts.
2. For idempotent operations (embeddings): safe to retry. For non-idempotent (billing-affecting) consider server-side idempotency keys.

3) API examples and canonical patterns
Provide complete examples for:
- REST: POST /v1/generate (request/response example)
- Websocket/Streaming: incremental tokens handling, reconnect policy
- Tool/Function calling: structured output schema example and validation guidance

REST example (curl)
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-compat-1","input":"Summarize the following..."}'
```

Streaming pattern (JS/TS)
- Use chunked responses and render partial tokens to UI.
- Maintain per-user sequence id for reconnection if streaming is interrupted.
- Fall back to truncated non-streaming response for low-bandwidth clients.

Function calling example (JSON schema snippet)
- Provide schema for expected output to validate model-provided arguments before executing side-effects.

4) Docs site operating procedures (process & checklist)
Process overview
- All new docs are authored in the docs repo and submitted by PR.
- PR must include a short summary, target audience, and test instructions.
- A reviewer from DevEx and one from the owning product team must approve.
- After merge, the docs site build is automatically triggered; staging preview is posted to PR.
- Roll to production once smoke tests pass in staging.

PR checklist (required)
- [ ] Title, summary, and audience defined
- [ ] Frontmatter metadata (title, author, created_at, last_updated, labels, related_pages)
- [ ] Code snippets have been linted and executed in CI
- [ ] Snippet outputs captured (where applicable) as fixtures
- [ ] Cross-links to related pages added
- [ ] Reviewer approvals (DevEx + product)
- [ ] Accessibility check for images and alt text

Versioning and deprecation
- Docs are versioned alongside public SDK release tags.
- When an API is deprecated, add a deprecation banner and migration guide.
- Deprecation policy: Mark deprecated for 90 days before removal; notify customers via changelog and email for breaking changes.

Publishing cadence
- Minor content updates: weekly (rolling deploys)
- Major guides or structural changes: coordinate with marketing and product, schedule a content freeze and release window.

Operational runbook for docs-site incidents
1. Detect: Pager alerts for build failures, staging preview errors, or broken public pages (404 spikes).
2. Triage: DevEx oncall claims and triages in #devex-docs with incident template.
3. Mitigate: Roll back to last good build or hotfix the docs repo.
4. Communicate: Post status to the status page and internal Slack.
5. Postmortem: Follow the standard incident-review template under oncall-and-incident-response.

5) Top support issues and canonical fixes
Preface: This section lists recurring developer support issues observed in the last 12 months with canonical triage steps and permanent remediations. Use this as first-pass when responding to tickets.

Table: Top issues (symptoms -> probable cause -> quick fix -> permanent fix -> owner)
| Issue | Symptoms | Probable cause | Quick fix (1-3 steps) | Permanent fix | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Authentication failures | 401 responses after valid key set | Old SDK defaulting to legacy auth header; environment variable not set in CI | 1) Verify REDWOOD_API_KEY is present 2) Show example of explicit client init | Release SDK patch fixing header fallback + CI templates update | DevEx / SDK team |
| 2. Streaming disconnects mid-response | Partial tokens, reconnects cause duplicated output | Client reconnect logic not de-duplicating or server-side timeout mismatch | 1) Advise client to use sequence IDs 2) Increase client-side buffer window | Add idempotent streaming tokens; update examples and retry guidance | Eng Serving Runtime |
| 3. High latency for short prompts | Long tail due to batching + cold KV cache | Small prompt routing into batch pipeline expecting larger payloads | 1) Recommend low-latency route param example ("latency_profile": "low") 2) Use pinned small-model for interactive paths | Add routing policy defaults and docs describing route profiles | Platform Routing Team |
| 4. Unexpected tokenization differences | Model output truncated or unexpected token counts | Mismatch between SDK tokenizer and model tokenizer version | 1) Recommend SDK tokenizer upgrade to vX.Y 2) Provide fallback detokenization script | Versioned tokenizer artifacts packaged with SDK releases | Applied ML / SDK |
| 5. Embeddings mismatch in search | Semantic search returns stale or low-recall results | Vector store index using older embedding model; missing reindex | 1) Confirm model used to generate index 2) Trigger reindex for changed model | Automate index versioning and reindex triggers; add audit logs | Customer Success + Eng Private Deploys |

Ticket triage template (copy into support replies)
1) Ask for reproducible snippet (language, SDK version, endpoint, minimal input)
2) Ask for full request/response (redacted API key) and headers (x-request-id, timestamp)
3) Advise steps already attempted and urgency (P0/P1/P2)
4) Provide immediate workaround from table above

Metrics and quality checks for docs
- PR review time: target <48 hours for non-blocking content updates
- Docs build success rate: >= 99.5% per week
- Staging preview availability: 100% for merged PRs within 10 minutes
- Support deflection: track ticket volume where KB article solved issue (target +20% YoY)

How to update this playbook
1. Create PR against docs repo and tag @devex for review.
2. Include changelog summary and affected quickstarts/guides.
3. Major structural changes require a short RFC and review by DevEx + product.
